title: The Writings of Clement of Alexandria, Vol. 1
author: Clement of Alexandria (Wilson trans)
description: The Writings of Clement of Alexandria, Volume 1, translated by William Wilson, in the Ante-Nicene Christian Library (Edinburgh: T. & T. Clark, 1867). Clement of Alexandria (c. 150-215), head of the catechetical school of Alexandria and teacher of Origen, sought to show that Christianity fulfils the best of Greek philosophy and presented the ideal Christian as the true 'gnostic'. This volume contains the Exhortation to the Heathen (Protrepticus), urging pagans to abandon the mysteries and idols for the Logos, with valuable descriptions of the Greek mystery cults; The Instructor (Paedagogus), in which Christ the Tutor guides the believer in daily conduct, diet, dress and manners; and the opening books of the Miscellanies (Stromata). It is a primary source on early Christian Platonism and the pagan mysteries.
